text: Trump Signals Possible US-Canada Trade Deal Soon President Donald Trump said the United States and Canada could reach a trade agreement “fairly soon,” signaling optimism after months of escalating tensions between the two countries. Trump said Canada wants a deal with Washington but insisted that Canadian tariffs on US farmers must be addressed, particularly what he described as duties as high as 400%. The trade dispute has expanded beyond tariffs, threatening cross-border supply chains and industries such as automobiles. After negotiations collapsed in August, both countries imposed additional tariffs and trade restrictions, raising concerns about higher prices and further economic disruption. Despite Trump’s latest comments, formal negotiations have yet to clearly resume, leaving uncertainty over whether the two sides can quickly reach a broader agreement.

text: Trump’s Ireland Visit Highlights Delicate US-Ireland Ties US President Donald Trump arrived in Ireland for a two-day visit, receiving a warm welcome from Irish leaders despite political tensions and public criticism surrounding his presidency. Trump is scheduled to meet Taoiseach Micheál Martin, with trade expected to be a key topic, while his itinerary also includes attending the Irish Open at his family’s golf resort in Doonbeg. Irish officials are seeking to maintain strong relations with Trump as Ireland’s economy remains closely linked to US investment and multinational companies. Although the visit is being presented as an opportunity to highlight longstanding ties between the two countries, disagreements over tariffs, trade balances, defense and US-European relations create diplomatic challenges for Dublin, particularly as Ireland currently holds the rotating presidency of the European Union.

text: BRICS Urges Restraint as Middle East Tensions Escalate BRICS nations, including Iran, the United Arab Emirates, India and China, have expressed deep concern over rising tensions in the Middle East and called for maximum restraint. In a joint statement, the group urged countries to avoid actions that could further worsen the conflict and encouraged dialogue and diplomacy to achieve lasting peace, security and stability. The escalating conflict has disrupted regional trade and pushed up global crude, fuel and gas prices, creating pressure for major energy importers such as India and China. BRICS also stressed the importance of maintaining the flow of global trade, energy and supply chains, particularly amid concerns over the Strait of Hormuz. The group condemned attacks on civilian infrastructure and peaceful nuclear facilities while calling for greater international cooperation to prevent further escalation.

text: Xi and Modi Move Toward Better Ties Chinese President Xi Jinping and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi met in New Delhi to improve relations between China and India. The two leaders discussed the border dispute, trade, supply chains and market access, and agreed to work toward a fair and mutually acceptable solution to the boundary issue. The meeting marks a positive step after years of tensions, especially following the 2020 border conflict. Both countries have recently taken steps to restore ties, including resuming direct flights and easing some investment restrictions, although differences and mutual distrust remain.

author: firstsquaw
text: Anthropic CEO Calls for Slower AI Development Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has called for the AI industry to slow the pace of developing new models, warning that rapidly advancing AI could create serious risks for humans. He pointed to AI’s growing ability to improve itself and recent incidents in which AI agents breached websites during testing. Amodei said slowing development does not mean stopping AI progress, but giving companies more time to improve safety and allow independent experts to evaluate their systems. He also called for cooperation across the industry and between countries, saying AI can greatly benefit society if it is developed carefully and responsibly.

text: California Diesel Prices Hit Record Highs Diesel prices in California have surged to record levels, with the statewide average rising above $8 a gallon and one San Diego station charging $9.99. Low fuel supplies, reduced refining capacity, limited pipelines and high state taxes are worsening the crisis, while global conflicts are putting further pressure on energy markets. The rising costs are hurting businesses that depend heavily on diesel, including trucking, moving and construction companies. Many are being forced to raise prices or accept lower profits as fuel expenses soar, adding to inflation and making everyday goods and services more expensive for consumers.

text: The biggest issue with an AI "safety slowdown:" What happens with China? While there are legitimate concerns around the safety of AI and how quickly it is evolving, the AI race is global. And, in today's ecosystem, falling even 6 months behind in the AI race is like falling decades behind in the pre-AI world. If US AI giants agree to slow progress and focus on safety, there must be an international agreement in place as well. And, even if there is an agreement in place, how do we regulate compliance? We've said it before and we will say it again: AI is the biggest technological revolution in history. This is an AI arms race that may be impossible to fully regulate.

author: firstsquaw
text: PRESIDENT DONALD TRUMP SAYS HE WILL REMOVE U.S. TARIFFS ON IRISH WHISKEY, ANNOUNCING THE MOVE SUNDAY AS HE ATTENDED A GOLF TOURNAMENT AT HIS FAMILY'S COURSE IN WESTERN IRELAND, TELLING THE CROWD 'ON BEHALF OF THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA, I AM GOING TO TAKE THE TARIFFS OFF', WITH IRISH WHISKEY AND OTHER EU GOODS GENERALLY SUBJECT TO A 10% TARIFF UNDER AN ADJUSTED RATE FOLLOWING A SUPREME COURT RULING STRIKING DOWN EARLIER LEVIES.

text: THE DECISION DELIVERS A MAJOR VICTORY TO THE IRISH GOVERNMENT AND HIGHLIGHTS TRUMP'S OFTEN SHIFTING AND PERSONAL APPROACH TO TRADE POLICY, COMING AT THE END OF A TWO-DAY VISIT IN WHICH IRELAND'S LEADERS 'ROLLED OUT THE RED CARPET', WITH TRUMP SAYING HE WAS BESIEGED BY REQUESTS TO ADDRESS THE WHISKEY LEVIES INCLUDING FROM IRISH PRIME MINISTER MICHEAL MARTIN AND GOLFER SHANE LOWRY.

text: 89% OF AMERICANS SAY GOVERNMENT CORRUPTION IS REAL — PUBLIC TRUST HITS A BREAKING POINT A striking 89% of Americans believe corruption is present in the U.S. government, highlighting a deep and widespread crisis of public trust. The figure reflects growing concerns that political institutions may be influenced by self-interest, special interests, or unethical behavior rather than serving the public fairly. The perception of corruption can have serious consequences for democracy, weakening confidence in elected officials and government institutions. While believing corruption exists does not necessarily mean that 89% of Americans believe the entire government is corrupt, the statistic signals a powerful demand for greater transparency, accountability, and ethical leadership.
